content: The following references and studies provide detailed insights into various aspects of iron metabolism, iron deficiency, and related health conditions: 1. A 2004 study in the Journal of Experimental Biology explored the properties of striated muscle, contributing to our understanding of muscle physiology. 2. Netz et al. (2014) discussed the maturation of cytosolic and nuclear iron-sulfur proteins in Trends in Cell Biology, highlighting the critical role of these proteins in cellular function. 3. Stevens et al. (2013) conducted a systematic analysis of global, regional, and national trends in hemoglobin concentration and anemia prevalence from 1995 to 2011, published in The Lancet Global Health. This study provided valuable data on anemia in children, pregnant women, and non-pregnant women. 4. Ganz (2013) reviewed systemic iron homeostasis in Physiological Reviews, emphasizing the mechanisms regulating iron levels in the body. 5. The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed tools for the prevention and control of nutritional anemias, accessible as of January 2020. 6. Verdon et al. (2003) conducted a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial on iron supplementation for unexplained fatigue in non-anemic women, published in BMJ. The study demonstrated the potential benefits of iron supplementation in this population. 7. Pasricha et al. (2014) performed a systematic review and meta-analysis on the benefits of iron supplementation for physical performance in women of reproductive age, published in The Journal of Nutrition. 8. Li et al. (1994) investigated the functional consequences of iron supplementation in iron-deficient female cotton mill workers in Beijing, China, as reported in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 9. Lozoff (2007) examined the impact of iron deficiency on child development in Food and Nutrition Bulletin, emphasizing the long-term effects of early-life iron deficiency. 10. Camaschella (2015) provided a comprehensive review of iron-deficiency anemia in the New England Journal of Medicine, discussing its causes, diagnosis, and treatment. 11. Papagiannakis et al. (2013) explored the role of Helicobacter pylori infection in hematological disorders in the European Journal of Internal Medicine. 12. The WHO guideline on the use of ferritin concentrations to assess iron status in individuals and populations was made available in January 2020. 13. Peeling et al. (2008) investigated athletic-induced iron deficiency and the role of inflammation, cytokines, and hormones in the European Journal of Applied Physiology. 14. Spencer (2013) raised concerns about the iron status of blood donors in Current Opinion in Hematology, questioning whether frequent donations lead to iron depletion. 15. Bull-Henry and Al-Kawas (2013) reviewed the evaluation of occult gastrointestinal bleeding in American Family Physician, providing diagnostic insights. 16. Kassebaum et al. (2014) conducted a systematic analysis of the global anemia burden from 1990 to 2010, published in Blood, offering a comprehensive overview of anemia trends. 17. Brissot et al. discussed the diagnosis and treatment of HFE-hemochromatosis in a chapter of a book on erythropoiesis and iron metabolism, accessed in January 2020. 18. Piga et al. evaluated and treated secondary iron overload in another chapter of the same book, emphasizing the management of iron-related disorders. 19. Bacon et al. (2011) provided practice guidelines for the diagnosis and management of hemochromatosis in Hepatology, issued by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases. 20. Baer et al. (1995) studied hemochromatosis screening in asymptomatic men aged 30 and older, as reported in the American Journal of Medicine. 21. Phatak et al. (1998) examined the prevalence of hereditary hemochromatosis in primary care patients in Annals of Internal Medicine. 22. Weatherall (2011) highlighted the global health burden of inherited hemoglobin disorders in the Indian Journal of Medical Research. 23. Jacobs (1977) discussed serum ferritin as an indicator of iron stores in Federation Proceedings. 24. Lipschitz et al. (1974) evaluated serum ferritin as a clinical index of iron stores in the New England Journal of Medicine. 25. Milman (1996) studied serum ferritin levels in Danes across different life stages and conditions, as reported in the International Journal of Hematology. 26. Milman et al. (1992) analyzed iron status markers in Danish women in relation to menstruation, hormonal contraception, and other factors in Annals of Hematology. 27. Nelson et al. (1978) assessed ferritin as an index of bone marrow iron stores in the Southern Medical Journal. 28. Walters et al. (1973) examined serum ferritin concentrations and iron stores in normal subjects in the Journal of Clinical Pathology. 29. Pasricha et al. (2010) provided a clinical update on the diagnosis and management of iron deficiency anemia in the Medical Journal of Australia. 30. The WHO guideline on ferritin concentrations for assessing iron status in populations was reviewed in January 2020. 31. Malempati et al. (2009) described bone marrow aspiration and biopsy procedures in the New England Journal of Medicine. 32. Riley et al. (2009) discussed the interpretation of bone marrow aspirates and biopsies in the Journal of Clinical Laboratory Analysis. 33. Bain and Bailey (2011) highlighted pitfalls in obtaining and interpreting bone marrow aspirates in the Journal of Clinical Pathology. 34. Conrad and Barton (1981) reviewed factors affecting iron balance in the American Journal of Hematology. 35. Deugnier and Turlin (2007) examined the pathology of hepatic iron overload in the World Journal of Gastroenterology. 36. Wood (2007) discussed the role of imaging in diagnosing and managing transfusion iron overload in the American Journal of Hematology. 37. Wood (2007) also reviewed magnetic resonance imaging for measuring iron overload in Current Opinion in Hematology. 38. St. Pierre et al. (2005) described methods for measuring and mapping liver iron concentrations using MRI in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences. 39. Garcia-Casal et al. (2014) proposed rethinking ferritin cutoffs for iron deficiency and overload in The Lancet Haematology. 40. Phiri et al. (2009) suggested new ferritin and soluble transferrin receptor cutoffs for assessing iron deficiency in children in high-infection areas, published in the Journal of Clinical Pathology. 41. Worwood (2000) provided indicators of iron status in populations in a WHO report. 42. Garcia-Casal et al. (2015) reviewed serum ferritin as an index of iron deficiency and overload in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 43. Blackmore et al. (2008) evaluated automated immunoassay methods for ferritin in Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine. 44. Thorpe et al. (1997) conducted an international study to evaluate a recombinant ferritin preparation as an international standard in Clinical Chemistry. 45. Hamwi et al. (2002) established reference values for ferritin assays in Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine. 46. The National Institute for Biological Standards and Control provided ferritin standards, accessed in January 2020. 47. The WHO guideline on ferritin concentrations for assessing iron status in populations was reviewed in January 2020. 48. De Maeyer (2000) offered guidance on preventing and controlling anemia through primary healthcare. 49. Mei et al. (2005) analyzed hemoglobin and ferritin as indicators of population response to iron interventions in the Journal of Nutrition. 50. A WHO report prioritized the assessment of vitamin A and iron status in populations. 51. The WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (21st edition) was reviewed in January 2020. 52. The WHO e-Library of Evidence for Nutrition Actions (eLENA) was accessed in January 2020. 53. The WHO bulletin and other resources were reviewed for evidence-based recommendations on ferritin concentrations and iron status. These references collectively provide a comprehensive understanding of iron metabolism, its clinical implications, and the tools available for diagnosis and management.
